FINAL_STATES: u3

(u2, door_open & !has_door_key) -> u2
(u2, door_open & target_picked_up) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, has_door_key, u2) -> 0.15
(u2, door_open & target_picked_up, u3) -> 1.0
feedback: FINAL_STATES header is present and u3 is accepting, but the RM fails the task's ordered-transition requirements. (1) Task requires holding the key on two or more different moves before picking up the box; the trace does this via u0→u1→u2 on has_door_key, which is plausible, but the u2 self-loop 'door_open & !has_door_key' fires while the key is still held (dropping the key with door open sets has_door_key false with door_open true, matching this predicate) — however there is no transition or reward acknowledging door_open itself, so the event of opening the door is invisible to the machine and 'door_open & target_picked_up' requires both on the same step, which cannot happen: after the door opens the agent must drop the key (has_door_key false) and then pick up the box, so door_open and target_picked_up do co-occur at pickup time (door still open) — this actually works. (2) Bigger problem: nothing forbids skipping the key-holding requirement in spirit — u0→u1→u2 needs has_door_key twice, fine. (3) But u2's 'door_open & !has_door_key' self-loop is not a transition on a progress event and merely self-loops; the machine never distinguishes door_open as a required intermediate milestone, so an episode that opens the door, drops the key, and picks up the box is covered only at the final pickup — acceptable for the final reward but the door-open milestone is unrewarded while key-holding is, making the dense progress scheme inconsistent and potentially reward-hacking (agent can farm the 0.15 by repeatedly picking up/dropping the key? No — dropping the key before door open fires key_lost but machine ignores it; farming is possible: u1 with has_door_key self-loops at u1, but the 0.15 fires only on u1→u2, once; the 0.1 fires once since returning to u0 requires... there is no transition back to u0, so farming is impossible). (4) Real blocker: the else self-loops at u0 and u1 do not cover key_lost and do not regress on key_lost; per the task/event semantics, dropping the key before opening the door should reset progress (explicit regression required where the task demands it — key_lost is defined precisely for this). The machine ignores key_lost entirely, so an agent that drops the key pre-door still holds u1/u2 progress incorrectly. (5) Missing reward on reaching u2's holding state after door_open is acceptable, but compactness is otherwise fine. Fix: add key_lost-driven regression transitions (u1→u0, u2→u0 on key_lost) and an explicit door_open transition out of the key-held state, with bounded dense rewards.

(u4, else) -> u4
(u5, else) -> u5
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key & !key_lost, u1) -> 0.15

(u1, key_lost, u0) -> 0.0
(u2, door_open & has_door_key, u3) -> 0.2

(u3, door_open & !has_door_key, u4) -> 0.2
(u4, door_open & target_picked_up, u5) -> 0.3
feedback: The RM mostly captures the task, but has structural and semantic problems. (1) The task says the agent must hold the key on two or more different moves — the (u1, has_door_key) self-loop structure is right, but u1→u2 on (has_door_key & !key_lost) creates a second reward of 0.15 for merely continuing to hold the key while also being the loop-guard state; the reward is given on the transition into u2, meaning progress is counted at the step the key is still held, which is acceptable, but see (2). (2) Semantic bug: u2's else self-loop does not include staying in u2 while the key remains held and the door not open; more importantly, u2 transitions to u3 only when door_open & has_door_key. But per the constraints, door_open can only become true while the key is held, so this is fine — however after door_open, if the agent keeps holding the key and toggles the door closed again (door_open false), u2 is no longer reachable: u2's only outgoing non-self transitions are door_open & has_door_key and key_lost. If in u3 (door open, key still held) the agent toggles the door shut (allowed, door_open turns false again and is never relocked), the machine is stuck in u3 forever since (door_open & !has_door_key) never becomes true while the key is held and dropping the key now makes door_open false at that same step? No — door_open stays true after the key is dropped, so u3→u4 remains reachable. But the reverse regression: in u4, if the door is toggled shut (door_open false), u4's only progress transition requires door_open & target_picked_up, which is impossible when the door is shut... except target_picked_up is unreachable with the door closed, so the agent would be stuck in u4 with no path back. A regression transition (u4, !door_open, ...) back to an earlier state (e.g. u2) is needed, since door_open can turn false again and the task requires recovery. (3) Regression from u1/u2 via key_lost resets to u0 — good — but there is no regression path from u3/u4 when the door is re-shut, as noted. (4) key_lost is correctly treated as a one-step event with explicit reset transitions and the per-state else self-loops cover irrelevant events — good. (5) Rewards are dense and bounded, but the u0→u1 and u1→u2 rewards give 0.3 total for holding the key twice while the u3→u4 (dropping the key with door open) gets 0.2; this is a design choice, not an error. (6) Ordering coverage: the trace requires key→door_open→drop key→pick box; u2 requires door_open & has_door_key, which holds at the toggle step — good. (7) FINAL_STATES header present and u5 declared and accepting. The blocking issue is the missing regression transition when door_open turns false in u4 (and possibly u3 with the key dropped), which makes the RM unsound for episodes where the agent toggles the door shut after opening it. Add explicit regression transitions for the door re-closing case and re-submit.

feedback: Reward machine evaluation: (1) Format is present, but the header lists states u0-u5 without explicit declarations. (2) 'FINAL_STATES: u5' is nonempty and u5 is accepting, satisfying the structural requirement. (3) States u1 and u2 correctly track the required 'hold the key on two or more different moves' progression via self-loops on 'has_door_key' and regression on 'key_lost'. (4) Transition coverage has significant semantic issues: in u3, `!door_open` is checked BEFORE `!has_door_key`. Since dropping the key occurs while the door is already open (per constraints, dropping the key to pick up the box happens after door_open), the agent in u3 will drop the key. If `door_open` remains true, `!door_open` is false, so it goes to u4 via `!has_door_key` — this is fine. However, if the door somehow becomes closed (relock not allowed per facts, but if door_open went false), u3 would go to u2 without accounting for `!has_door_key` correctly. (5) In u4, the condition `door_open & target_picked_up` is safe since target_picked_up implies door_open. But there is no path to handle `target_picked_up` directly if the agent somehow reaches u4 without door_open true — although this violates environment constraints, the RM doesn't enforce the `door_open` precondition for picking up the box robustly here. (6) Missing coverage of irrelevant events/per-state else loops is mostly handled but the priority ordering in u3/u4 might cause a regression to u2 when the agent drops the key if `!door_open` triggers before `!has_door_key` in the same step. Specifically, if the agent drops the key and the door is somehow closed simultaneously, the agent is sent to u2, but `!has_door_key` is also true, potentially missing the intended u4 transition. (7) Crucially, the transition `!door_open -> u2` from u3/u4 represents a regression, but there is no explicit regression from u4 back to u3/u2 if the agent drops the box (though constraints say they cannot relock, they could drop the box after picking it up — however, picking up the box terminates the episode per facts). (8) Rewards are bounded and dense but the progression in u0 -> u1 -> u2 rewards identical steps (0.1 and 0.2) which is acceptable. Rejecting primarily due to unhandled precedence in transition guards and lack of explicit state declarations in the header.

feedback: The RM correctly encodes the task: holding the key across two distinct steps (u0→u1→u2 on consecutive has_door_key steps) then reaching the box (u2→u3→u4→u5). Semantic fidelity: predicates match the environment definitions; the self-loop structure avoids relying on forbidden co-holds. Reachability: u5 is reachable exactly via key held two steps, door opened, key dropped, box picked up — consistent with the constraint that the key must be dropped after door_open before pickup (u3→u4 requires !has_door_key with door_open, and that drop is correctly not key_lost). Compactness: 6 states is minimal for the two-step key-hold requirement plus door and drop phases. Predicate-only events: key_lost is the only event and is handled correctly as a one-step regression (u1/u2 → u0) plus its exclusion from other guard conjunctions where required (e.g. u3's progress guard omits key_lost, but key_lost cannot co-occur with door_open anyway per constraints, so no hole; per-state else self-loops cover all irrelevant events). Persistent/event distinctions: door_open is treated as persistent with explicit regression via else-transitions back to u2 when it turns false; key_lost is treated as an event (single-step transition), matching the environment's declared event reading. Ordered transition coverage: transitions are ordered so regression paths (key_lost → u0) are checked before else self-loops, and u3/u4 check regression before progress where they share conditions — no shadowing issues since guards are mutually disjoint or regression-checked first. Reward safety: progress rewards 0.1–0.25 are sparse-to-dense but bounded, with 1.0 at the final transition; regressions to u0 yield no reward, so there is no reward farming by re-earning progress (dropping the key resets to u0 and rewards must be re-earned, which is safe). FINAL_STATES header present with u5, declared in STATES and accepting as the terminal for the task. Minor note: u1's else self-loop means a door_open-without-key event cannot occur per constraints, so no coverage gap. Overall a faithful, safe, and compact RM.

All four declared propositions are implemented exactly as specified, with no extra predicates, imports, or side effects. `has_door_key` checks that the agent carries a key whose color matches the door found in the grid; `door_open` scans for an open door; `target_picked_up` matches the carried box against the mission string; `key_lost` is correctly read as an event, comparing the previous step's `has_door_key` valuation with the current key and door state, and is false otherwise. The grid scan guards empty cells, uses only the documented API (`env.carrying`, `env.grid.get`, `env.width`, `env.height`, `env.mission`, object `type`/`color`/`is_open`), and reads `episode_memory['previous_valuation']` without mutation. Syntax is valid and semantics align with the constraints (key_lost excludes has_door_key and door_open by construction).
